data.ruling: The refutation stands. P2's own found answer to V75 says both faults are continuous: a short to ground, and a short to the port's supply pin at up to 8.7 V (F16). The lower bounds come from 3.3 V / 12 mA and 3.4 V / 24 mA, so they only cover a line driven high into a short to ground. The 8.7 V figures (18.5 mA, 95 mW) only cover the current into a 3.6 V clamp. Now take a line the element drives low while it is shorted to 8.7 V. The node sits at the driver's output-low voltage (VOL), below the clamp, so the clamp does not conduct and the full (8.7 V - VOL)/R flows into the driver. On a line an SN74LVC244A drives through 142 Ohm, that is 57.4 mA at VOL 0.55 V, or 61 mA at 0 V. That is above the absolute-maximum continuous output current of +-50 mA (SCAS414AG 5.1), not only above the recommended 24 mA (5.3). On a pad-driven line through 275 Ohm, it is 29.8 mA at VOL 0.5 V, or 31.6 mA at 0 V. That is above the 12 mA the claim itself uses as its bound. The RP2350 datasheet characterises VOL only up to 12 mA and says the drive modes are not hard limits. The resistor then dissipates 8.2^2/275 = 244 mW, not 95 mW. To keep this fault within those limits, the bounds must be at least 683 Ohm on pad lines ((8.7 - 0.5)/12 mA; 725 Ohm at VOL 0) and at least 340 Ohm on 244 lines ((8.7 - 0.55)/24 mA). Using the claim's own servo-configuration formula with the servo's output-low voltage Vs = 0, 3.3/1000 / (1/1000 + 1/10000 + 1/R) <= 0.8 V gives R <= 330.6 Ohm. So on the pad-driven multiprotocol and UART lines the fault bound is higher than that ceiling. The figure as stated is not a valid range for the fault set it names. The scope is function: this is about the function's requirement value, not about any part.
data.evidence: SCAS414AG (revised June 2026) section 5.1: IO continuous output current +-50 mA; section 5.3: IOL 24 mA at VCC 3 V; electrical characteristics: VOL 0.55 V max at IOL 24 mA, VCC 3 V. RP2350 datasheet, build-date 2025-07-29 (served as RP-008373-DS-2), Table 1436: VOL 0 to 0.5 V at IOVDD 3.3 V for IOL = 2, 4, 8 or 12 mA depending on setting; IIOVSS_MAX 100 mA total sunk into GPIO. Section 14.9.4 text: the 2/4/8/12 mA modes 'are not hard limits'. P2's V75 answer in FU-A2/004-P2-R4.json: 'Both faults, continuous ... a short to the port's supply pin at up to 8.7 V'; bounds 275 Ohm (3.3 V / 12 mA) and 142 Ohm (3.4 V / 24 mA); '(8.7 - 3.6) / 275 = 18.5 mA into a 3.6 V clamp and 95 mW'; servo formula V = (3.3/1000 + Vs/R) / (1/1000 + 1/10000 + 1/R). Arithmetic: 8.15/142 = 57.4 mA; 8.7/142 = 61.3 mA; 8.2/275 = 29.8 mA; 8.7/275 = 31.6 mA; 8.2^2/275 = 244 mW; 8.2/0.012 = 683 Ohm; 8.15/0.024 = 340 Ohm; the ceiling at Vs = 0 is 330.6 Ohm. IOBoard.md:536 at e13f5f60: 'No requirement in the tree limits the current into a shorted signal line at an output connector.' F16: HV ceiling 8.7 V.
